model.rationale: Clyburn pairs a solidly Democratic district with unmatched name recognition and a dominant financial position against a challenger showing no reported fundraising, and markets price his reelection near 97 percent. The genuine uncertainty is only the size of the margin, since no polls test the race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the district far narrower than its partisan lean, or a sudden influx of outside spending for Peterson, would be the signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District leans Democratic by about thirteen points, and Jim Clyburn has held the seat since 1993, giving him deep name recognition and a loyal constituency. He enters the general election with roughly $1.6 million on hand after raising $1.2 million, while Republican John Peterson shows no reported fundraising. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets put Clyburn's chances near 97 percent, in line with the district's fundamentals. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the exact margin open to question even though the direction of the outcome is not. A Republican upset would require a dramatic, currently unobserved shift in the district's partisan balance or an external wave far beyond what any available evidence suggests.
